# OKX public fixtures

Collected 2026-11-05 UTC, unauthenticated HTTPS from OKX official sources.

- `announcements.json`: complete first page of `GET https://www.okx.com/api/v5/support/announcements?annType=announcements-delistings&page=1`, `Accept-Language: en-US`. API contract: https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/en/#announcement-get-announcements. 20 entries/page, `totalPage=7`, business code `0`; five requests/two seconds/IP. Public results are region/IP dependent. `pTime` is original publication milliseconds; `businessPTime` is displayed publication time. No authentication headers are sent.
- `spot_article.html`: only the rendered `<article>` from https://www.okx.com/help/okx-to-delist-dora-icx-storj-zeus-and-elf-spot-trading-pairs. The SSR `article div[class*='richTextContent']` contains the original table, including USDC/EUR September 30 deadlines and separate USDT October 3 deadlines. Navigation, scripts and footers are unnecessary for parsing and omitted.
- `swap_article.html`: only the rendered `<article>` from https://www.okx.com/help/okx-to-delist-perpetual-futures-for-icxusdt. September 17 08:00 UTC settlement, cancel orders and mandatory close; no separate reduce-only deadline is invented.
- `swap_instruments.json`: two unchanged rows (BTC-USDT-SWAP and BTC-USD-SWAP) selected from the successful complete `GET https://www.okx.com/api/v5/public/instruments?instType=SWAP` response. The fixture is a parser/filter sample, not a full production catalog. Contract: https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/en/#public-data-rest-api-get-instruments. The endpoint has no paging; limit is 20 requests/two seconds/IP/instrument type. `expTime` is expiry/delisting milliseconds for SWAP and SPOT; empty is unset. `live` is tradable; `suspend`, `preopen`, `test` and unrecognized states do not prove permanent removal. USDT linear perpetuals and USDT spot are the supported market scopes.

Malformed, empty, throttled, mismatched-market, future-expiry, elapsed-expiry and suspended-state cases are constructed in the corresponding unit tests. These fixtures contain public exchange information only. LLM normalization tests verify the two-cutoff data contract; they do not claim to validate a live model response.
